keyClass.description: Privacy class of the business key, as in key.class. business_code (default) shows it in clear; a value class tokenises it everywhere it appears: node business_key, edge endpoints, json_pointer member keys, root-cause keys, reports and chat.

attributes.description: Node members compared as element fields. Default: every emitted member other than type, the namespace field and the businessKey fields.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy codes for nodes of this type present on one side only. Defaults MISSING_NODE / EXTRA_NODE; a domain pack may map them to its own codes.

missing_in_b.description: Code when a node is in a but not in b.

extra_in_b.description: Code when a node is in b but not in a.

severity.description: Severity of one-sided nodes of this type.

graphEdgeType.description: One edge type of canonical graph mode (graph/v1). Edge key = [from, type, to, qualifier].

type.description: Edge type name; emitted edges carry it in their type member.

from.description: Node type of the from endpoint (declared in canonical.nodes; loader check).

to.description: Node type of the to endpoint (declared in canonical.nodes; loader check).

directed.description: Required. true: from -> to is significant. false: the edge is undirected, and its endpoints are sorted by node key before the edge key is built, so either emission order yields the same key.

qualifier.description: Member of each emitted edge that distinguishes parallel edges of the same type between the same endpoints (for example a relationship role). It becomes the fourth key component. Without a qualifier, parallel edges are compared as a multiset: only their count per (from, type, to) matters.

attributes.description: Edge members compared as element fields (edge properties). Default: every emitted member other than type, from, to and the qualifier.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy codes for edges of this type present on one side only. Defaults MISSING_EDGE / EXTRA_EDGE; a domain pack may map them to its own codes (for example MISSING_LINK).

missing_in_b.description: Code when an edge is in a but not in b.

extra_in_b.description: Code when an edge is in b but not in a.

severity.description: Severity of one-sided edges of this type.

graphScope.description: Graph scope: the root, the edge types followed, the direction and the depth. Elements outside scope are dropped on both sides before the diff, and cycles are bounded by visited node keys. Scope is a selection predicate: an element inside scope on one side but outside it on the other (for example at depth 1 on a and depth 2 on b) is a FILTER_MEMBERSHIP finding, not MISSING_* / EXTRA_*.

root.description: Root node: the node of this type whose business key equals the canonical comparison key (key.name after key.normalize and the type's keyNormalize).

namespace.description: Namespace of the root node; needed only when the root type uses namespaceField.

edgeTypes.description: Edge types followed from the root. Default: every declared edge type.

direction.description: Direction in which directed edges are followed: out (from -> to), in (to -> from) or both (default). Undirected edge types are followed both ways.

depth.description: Maximum hops from the root. Always bounded: reachability and path enumeration never go further.

key.description: Ordered components of a canonical node key: [type, namespace, business_key] (default) or [tenant, type, namespace, business_key] in a multi-tenant deployment, where tenant defaults to the deployment tenant. Used for graph-mode node keys and for crosswalk rows.

crosswalk.description: Reviewed identity crosswalk: a mapping table that translates side-specific source ids (for example a new platform's customer UUIDs) into canonical identity components, read through an approved SELECT template. The template returns one row per mapping with columns side ('a' | 'b'), type, source_id, namespace and business_key (plus tenant when identity.key uses it). It is pinned (SHA-256 and row count), so every key of a run, or of one soak cycle, uses the same mapping. Under time.mode frozen the crosswalk must be read from inside the run's EnvironmentSnapshot (a restored clone) or through a template that queries it AS OF the cut time T, and its SHA-256, row count and as_of are recorded in runs.cut_metadata; otherwise the run's claim level is observed. Live and soak runs re-read and re-pin it every cycle. Lookups are by (side, type, source_id). A source id with no row, a source id with several rows (ambiguous) and two source ids that map to the same key on one side (colliding) all make the key INCONCLUSIVE with inconclusive_reason identity_ambiguous; a crosswalk never merges entities. In graph mode, emitted nodes and edge endpoints that carry source_id are resolved automatically; in tree mode, resolve lists the canonical paths whose values are source ids.

target.description: Database target id holding the crosswalk table; read in a READ ONLY transaction. Under time.mode frozen it must be inside the run's EnvironmentSnapshot unless the template reads the table AS OF T.

template.description: Approved SELECT template returning the crosswalk rows.

resolve.description: Tree mode: canonical paths whose values on one side are source ids, replaced by the resolved business key before diffing.

side.description: Side whose values at path are source ids.

path.description: Canonical path pattern (path_pattern form) of the source-id values.

type.description: Entity type used for the lookup (the crosswalk type column).

inferredSchema.description: Approved inferred schema: a bundle with one JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) per side, keyed a and b, for that side's raw response before select/map, annotated with x-ds-* keywords (x-ds-array-mode ordered | set | multiset | keyed, x-ds-array-keys, x-ds-map, x-ds-align, x-ds-normalize) in the style of Kubernetes x-kubernetes-list-type / x-kubernetes-list-map-keys. ds-profiler drafts it from dry-run and calibration samples and a human approves it; compare.arrays and map rules are generated from its annotations. The spec only references the bundle, by ref, by digest or by both (then the digest must match the referenced bundle). The digest is part of the spec content_hash, so a changed inference makes a new spec version. Inline x-ds-* members are recorded, not validated deeply.

ref.description: Registry reference name@version of the approved bundle in ds.inferred_schemas, or an s3:// URI in the deployment object store.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the bundle's canonical encoding, written sha256:<64 lower-case hex digits>.

^x-ds-[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$.description: Inline x-ds-* annotation (for example a summary of x-ds-array-keys by path), recorded verbatim for review and covered by content_hash. It is not validated deeply, and the engine always reads the annotations from the referenced bundle.

schemaDrift.description: Schema guard for table sides (docs/mvp/PRECHECKS.md §7). At a run's creation, at each scan pass, at a key-list cycle's start, at a resume and after a failed read, each table side's catalogue entry (column names, declared types, classes, nullability, the primary key and the relation's kind) is checked against the one the run was planned on and, at creation, against the one the version's newest earlier run read. A change that alters what the plan's statements read or how a key renders always pauses the run; a new run that would not compare what its predecessor compared is created paused. mode says what any other change does. The inferred-schema guard for service sides (validating each observation against inferredSchema) is not built: schemaDrift acts on table sides only, and the per-key reason schema_drift and the SCHEMA_DRIFT finding stay unused.

mode.description: finding (default): a change that breaks nothing is recorded with a warning and the run goes on with its plan. pause: any change pauses the run (pause reason run_paused_schema_drift) until a person resumes it, which accepts the tables as they are, and a new run that would not compare what its predecessor compared is refused. A spec without a table side may not ask for pause.
